summary_of_work: **Category:** Derivation **Description:** Overview The returned data are measures of a blood-based biomarker for Alzheimer’s disease neuropathology called p-tau 217. Plasma samples collected at 69-year home visits were assayed using the ALZpath Simoa p-tau 217 assay version 2 at the UK DRI Biomarker Factory at UCL in spring 2024. 952 samples were assayed: this subset of approximately half of  all available 69-year home visit plasma samples was selected to prioritise assaying of samples from participants who had not enrolled in Insight 46 phases 1 and 2 (in which plasma p-tau 217 had already been measured). In samples from those who had not attended Insight 46 phases 1 and 2, there was also preferential selection for individuals who had died following the 69-year home visits, in order to ascertain p-tau 217 concentrations for individuals who would have no prospect of joining Insight 46 during phase 3 (where p-tau 217 assaying is planned).

categories: Imaging outcome measure – normal appering white mtter (NAWM)  diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) parameters indexing microstructural integrity including: 1. fractional anisotropy (FA) 2.  mean diffusivity (MD) 3. neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging (NODDI) derived parameters of neurite density index (NDI) 4. neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging (NODDI) derived parameters of orientation dispersion index (ODI) Alterations of NAWM integrity can be assessed by diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) which enables sensitive estimation of white matter tissue microstructure environments using water diffusion properties. Parameters typically include fractional anisotropy (FA), a measure of directionality, and mean diffusivity (MD), a measure of magnitude of diffusion. Additional multicompartmental modelling techniques have been developed to address limitations in these conventional measures. For example, neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging (NODDI) estimates microstructural complexity parameters of neurite density index (NDI), a measure of fraction of axons and dendrites; and orientation dispersion index (ODI), a measure of variability of neurite orientation (5). Lower values for FA and NDI and higher values for MD and ODI are thought to represent worse microstructural integrity.
